There are a couple of rainbows that break out of the current flat boring image and are very detailed and deep.

posts.author: Dinesh
posts.content_md:
[quote:3ddd662238]I remembered someone on the old board mentioning them and wondering who made the holograms. [/quote:3ddd662238]

That was me. I brought them to Texas, in fact. The hologram credit simply says: "Holograms created by OPSEC PLC - United Kingdom. Designed by Mike Jolley" I also have one called "The Ghost Pirates - A Spirited Hologram Book" This has holograms just as impressive but with no holographic credits at all and is printed in China. For those interested, it's published by Dial Books, A division of Penguin Books, 375 Hudson St, NY, NY 10014 and manufactured in China (no further address given). The ISBN seems to be: 13579108642, if this makes any sense. There's no specific mention of ISBN, but these numbers simply appear on a line of their own. Library of Congress Card no. : 95-6312.

A while back someone gave an informative report on his visit to the museum in Chicago. He also bemoaned the lack of credits on any of the holograms. As I said at the time, this is even worse in publishing, the fact that the holographic company is even mentioned is pretty rare.
